patients.summary: Retired administrative assistant with two breast cancers (left 2018, right ER-positive 2021 treated through mastectomy, docetaxel/carboplatin and tamoxifen) who joins in October 2022. Over four years she has HRT-related complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia ending in hysterectomy, recurrent depression, post-mastectomy shoulder and chest wall problems, worsening chemotherapy neuropathy, then liver metastases in 2025 and bilateral adrenal metastases with primary adrenal insufficiency in 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
56F joining us; wants a PCP close to home who can coordinate around her oncology care. Brought her bottles and a treatment summary.

ONC HX (per pt and the summary she brought; formal records requested)
- L breast: stage II IDC 2018. Lumpectomy + sentinel node bx, then adjuvant chemo. No evidence of disease since.
- R breast: stage IIA, ER+, 2021. Lumpectomy + radiation, then R modified radical mastectomy with axillary dissection early this year. Chemo after that through a port: docetaxel and carboplatin, finished in the spring. Port came out over the summer.
- Tamoxifen 20 daily since June. Tolerating it. Med onc follows her every few months.
- Since chemo the tips of her toes have been a little numb. Not painful, not affecting walking.

OTHER PMH
- Osteopenia on a DXA at her old office (2021). On calcium/D.
- One episode of depression years ago, resolved; no treatment now, no psychiatric admissions.
- Gallbladder out laparoscopically long ago.

MEDS: tamoxifen 20 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg/vit D3 400 IU BID; ibuprofen 400 mg q8h prn aches; MVI daily.
ALL: NKDA.
FH: mother - breast ca at 45, deceased. Maternal aunt - ovarian ca. Father - HTN, T2DM.
SH: divorced, lives alone in Northampton. Retired admin assistant. Never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses a MONTH. No drugs.

ROS: energy decent. No new lumps, no bone pain, no cough, no abdominal pain, no bleeding. Mood good.
PHQ-9 3.

EXAM: vitals in flowsheet, normal. Comfortable, well-groomed. HEENT unremarkable. No cervical, supraclavicular or L axillary nodes. R chest: well-healed mastectomy scar, flat, no nodularity, no skin change. L breast: healed lumpectomy scar, no mass, no nipple change. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars, no organomegaly. Arms: no lymphedema either side. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites.

A/P
1. R breast ca, ER+, on adjuvant tamoxifen - per oncology. Will get their notes.
2. Hx L breast ca - in remission.
3. Mild chemo neuropathy, toes - stable, observe.
4. Osteopenia - continue Ca/D. Old DXA requested.
5. HCM: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH; one-time HCV and HIV screening. Flu shot today. Colonoscopy and Pap history from old office pending records.
RTC 6-7 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Oncology treatment summary
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical Oncology - Treatment Summary (prepared 08/2022, sent at patient request)

Patient: Janet Madden, DOB 10/12/1965

Diagnoses:
1. Left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, stage II (2018). Lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. No evidence of recurrence.
2. Right breast carcinoma, stage IIA, ER positive (2021). Lumpectomy with adjuvant whole-breast radiation. Subsequent right modified radical mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection (02/2022). Implanted port placed; adjuvant docetaxel and carboplatin completed spring 2022; port removed 08/2022. Tamoxifen 20 mg daily started 06/2022, planned for at least 5 years.

Toxicities: grade 1 sensory neuropathy of the toes after docetaxel/carboplatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Surveillance: oncology visits every 3-6 months, annual left diagnostic mammogram.

documents.title: Gynecology visit letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Women's Health / Gynecology
Visit date: 02/06/2023

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Madden, 57, for vasomotor symptoms. For roughly the past year her cycles have been irregular and she now has severe hot flashes through the day and night sweats that wake her most nights. Allergies: none known.

After discussion she wished to start hormone therapy. I have prescribed estradiol 1 mg orally daily with micronized progesterone 100 mg nightly for endometrial protection.

Impression: perimenopausal vasomotor syndrome.
Plan: start combined therapy as above; follow up as needed or sooner with any bleeding.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

documents.title: Breast surgery follow-up letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Surgical Oncology / Breast Surgery
Date of visit: 02/27/2023
Re: Janet Madden, DOB 10/12/1965

Ms. Madden returns for routine surveillance, now about a year out from her right modified radical mastectomy with axillary dissection. Overall she is doing well and has recovered steadily. The chest wall itself is comfortable, with no pain and no swelling. Her complaint is an intermittent ache in the right upper back and difficulty working overhead, for example lifting things onto a high shelf.

Medications: tamoxifen 20 mg daily, estradiol 1 mg daily, micronized progesterone 100 mg nightly, calcium/vitamin D, ibuprofen as needed, multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Examination: The mastectomy flap is healed without erythema, warmth or swelling. Upper extremity range of motion is full bilaterally. When she leans into the wall with both arms extended, the medial edge of the right scapula stands out noticeably from the chest wall. Strength is 5/5 throughout the upper limbs apart from mild weakness of right shoulder abduction above 90 degrees. Sensation is normal in both arms and hands.

Impression: Post-surgical thoracic outlet syndrome, right.

Plan: Referral to physical therapy for scapular stabilization and shoulder girdle strengthening. Continue surveillance per medical oncology. Return in one year, sooner if needed.

Breast Surgery

documents.title: Physical therapy evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient Physical Therapy - Initial Evaluation (03/16/2023)
Referral: breast surgery, post-surgical thoracic outlet syndrome R.

S: Intermittent R upper back ache, trouble reaching overhead. No arm swelling.
O: Full AROM both shoulders. R scapular prominence with wall push-up. Mild R abduction weakness above shoulder height. Sensation intact.
A: Scapular stabilizer and shoulder girdle weakness after R mastectomy/ALND, consistent with referral diagnosis. Good rehab potential.
P: 6 visits over 6 weeks; serratus and lower trap strengthening, posture work; home exercise program issued today with band.

events.reason: Abnormal uterine bleeding on hormone therapy

reports.text:
Transabdominal and transvaginal pelvic ultrasound.
Indication: abnormal uterine bleeding on estrogen therapy.
Uterus: anteverted, smooth contour, no focal myometrial mass. Endometrium: thickened, measuring 14 mm in double-layer thickness, without focal lesion or fluid. Right and left ovaries: normal size and appearance. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Thickened endometrium, 14 mm. Otherwise normal pelvic ultrasound.

documents.title: Gynecology visit letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Women's Health / Gynecology
Visit date: 06/07/2023

Dear colleague,

Ms. Madden, now 57, returned with abnormal bleeding. She has been perimenopausal for about a year and started hormone therapy four months ago for severe vasomotor symptoms. She was on estradiol with micronized progesterone but stopped the progesterone on her own because of mood swings. For several weeks now she has had intermittent heavy bleeding. Current medications: estradiol 1 mg daily, tamoxifen 20 mg daily (oncology), calcium/vitamin D, ibuprofen as needed, multivitamin. NKDA.

Pelvic examination: unremarkable. Her most recent Pap was normal.
Pelvic ultrasound today: endometrium thickened at 14 mm; uterus and ovaries otherwise normal.

Impression: Endometrial hyperplasia, presumed, in the setting of hormone therapy.
Plan: endometrial sampling at a follow-up visit.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

reports.text:
Left diagnostic mammogram, CC, MLO and spot compression views of the lumpectomy site. History: left lumpectomy 2018, right mastectomy 2022.
Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. Post-lumpectomy architectural distortion and scar at the upper outer left breast, stable compared with prior outside studies. No suspicious mass, calcifications or new distortion. Skin and nipple unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 2: benign post-surgical changes. Annual follow-up.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, losing weight, not herself.

HPI: Since around early June she has been worn out all the time, sleeping badly (up at 3 am, can't get back to sleep), and has lost about 10 lb without trying (72.0 kg in Oct, 67.5 today). Feels low most of the day, most days. Has stopped going out to the garden, which is usually what she lives for in summer. Says she feels useless, and can't keep her mind on a book or a TV show. No thoughts of self-harm, no plan, no intent; feels safe. Feels it is like the episode she had years ago and wants to go back to psychiatry. No fever, no cough, no night sweats now. Still having intermittent bleeding; gyn plans a biopsy. Appetite down.
PHQ-9 16 (item 9 = 0).

Meds: tamoxifen, estradiol, Ca/D, ibuprofen prn, MVI.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Tired-appearing, subdued, linear thought, good eye contact. No nodes. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass. R chest wall unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Recurrent depressive symptoms, moderate. Psych referral (she prefers the psychiatry group she saw before). Safety plan reviewed; crisis line numbers given.
2. Fatigue/weight loss: CBC, CMP, TSH today.
3. Ongoing uterine bleeding - gyn following.
RTC after psychiatry.

documents.title: Lab results to patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Janet, your thyroid is normal (TSH 2.5) and your kidney, liver and salt levels are all fine. Your hemoglobin is mildly low at 11.2; white count and platelets are normal. We'll recheck the blood count at your physical in October. I've sent these results to psychiatry for your visit.

documents.title: Psychiatry evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry - Return Evaluation
Date seen: 09/04/2023
Referred by: primary care

Ms. Madden, 57, is known to our clinic from a prior depressive episode. She comes back now during a difficult stretch: ongoing gynecologic evaluation for abnormal bleeding and continuing endocrine therapy for breast cancer. Over three months she describes fatigue that does not lift, about ten pounds of unintended weight loss and broken sleep. Her mood is low for most of nearly every day. Gardening, her main pleasure, no longer interests her. She endorses feelings of worthlessness and poor concentration. No suicidal ideation. No fever, cough or other acute symptoms.

Medications: tamoxifen 20 mg daily, estradiol 1 mg daily, calcium/vitamin D, ibuprofen PRN, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: unremarkable apart from mild pallor. MSE: casually dressed, cooperative, mood 'low', affect congruent, thought process linear, no SI/HI, insight and judgment good.

Labs from primary care (08/22): Hgb 11.2, WBC 5.0, platelets 250, TSH 2.5, CMP normal.

Assessment: Major depressive disorder, recurrent episode, moderate.

Plan: Start escitalopram 10 mg daily (chosen to avoid interaction with tamoxifen). Referral for weekly psychotherapy. Follow-up here in 6 weeks; primary care may continue refills once stable.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update: I started the escitalopram two weeks ago and I have my first counseling appointment next Thursday. Too soon to tell but I'm sleeping a little better. Thank you for getting me in.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it, Janet. It usually takes 4-6 weeks to feel the full effect, so hang in there. See you on October 10.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL - 57F (58 on Thursday).

Interval: psychiatry started escitalopram 10 early Sept, in weekly counseling. Mood 'coming up out of the hole' - sleeping through most nights, out in the garden putting beds to bed for winter. PHQ-9 10 (from 16). Still some intermittent bleeding; gyn biopsy planned. Shoulder fine with home exercises. Toes unchanged.

Meds: tamoxifen 20, estradiol 1, escitalopram 10, Ca/D BID, ibuprofen prn, MVI. NKDA.
Habits: never smoker, wine a couple times a month, walks 30 min most days.

Screening/prevention:
- Colon: colonoscopy 2019 normal -> 2029.
- Cervical: Pap/HPV 2021 normal.
- Breast: L diagnostic mammo 6/2023 benign (oncology).
- Bone: osteopenia, on Ca/D.
- HCV/HIV done 2022.
- Vaccines today: flu, updated COVID, Shingrix #2, PCV20 (indicated with her cancer/chemo history). Tdap 2016.

Exam: vitals normal (see flowsheet). Pleasant, brighter than August. Eyes, ears, mouth normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly, no nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. R chest wall flat scar, no nodules. L breast no mass. Abdomen soft, no HSM. No edema. Feet: monofilament intact.

A/P:
1. MDD, recurrent - improving on escitalopram + therapy. Continue.
2. Mild anemia in Aug - recheck CBC today.
3. Breast ca on tamoxifen - per onc.
4. AUB - gyn.
5. HCM as above; lipids today (A1c normal last year).
RTC 6 wk telehealth for mood.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is at home, consented to virtual visit.
Mood follow-up. 10 weeks on escitalopram 10, counseling every other week now. Energy better, eating normally, concentrating enough to read again. Some sad days but no longer most days. No SI. No side effects she can name. Saw psychiatry in October - continue same dose; they're happy for us to refill.
PHQ-9 7.
Appears well on camera, smiling, normal speech.

reports.text:
Specimen: endometrium, office biopsy (pipelle).
Gross: received in formalin, multiple fragments of tan-red tissue aggregating 1.6 x 1.0 x 0.3 cm, entirely submitted.
Microscopic: crowded, back-to-back endometrial glands with complex architecture and cytologic atypia, with little intervening stroma. No stromal invasion identified. No carcinoma seen in this sample.
reports.conclusion: Endometrium, biopsy: complex atypical hyperplasia. Negative for carcinoma in this sample.

documents.title: Gynecology visit and biopsy result
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Women's Health / Gynecology
Visit date: 12/15/2023; pathology reviewed 12/19/2023

Dear colleague,

Ms. Madden returned with six months of intermittent vaginal bleeding since starting estrogen therapy, previously evaluated here with a thickened endometrium. She is not sexually active and has no discharge or pelvic pain. Her last Pap, two years ago, was normal. History is notable for stage IIA ER-positive right breast cancer treated with lumpectomy and radiation and then adjuvant tamoxifen, started 18 months ago. Medications: tamoxifen 20 mg, estradiol 1 mg daily (estrogen only since April), escitalopram 10 mg, calcium/vitamin D, ibuprofen PRN, multivitamin. NKDA.

Vital signs normal. Abdomen benign. Pelvic exam: uterus slightly enlarged and non-tender; no adnexal mass.

Labs: Hgb 12.3, platelets 250. FSH 7.2 mIU/mL, LH 6.9 mIU/mL, estradiol 45 pg/mL, in keeping with her oral estradiol.

Endometrial biopsy performed in the office. Pathology: complex atypical hyperplasia, no carcinoma in the sample.

Impression: complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

Plan: I called her on 12/19 with the result. Estradiol stopped as of that day. I have recommended total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and she agrees; we will schedule for early February. Please complete a pre-operative evaluation in January.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

documents.title: Hysterectomy?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The gynecologist called - the biopsy showed atypical hyperplasia and she wants to take out my uterus and ovaries in February. I stopped the estradiol Tuesday like she said. Honestly after everything else I just want to know if you think this is the right call.

documents.title: RE: Hysterectomy?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Janet, I'm sorry this is one more thing. Yes - with atypical hyperplasia, removing the uterus is the standard recommendation, and taking the ovaries at the same time makes sense with your breast cancer history. I agree with her. I've taken estradiol off your list. Our front desk will call you to set up the pre-op visit in January. The hot flashes may come back off the estradiol; tell me if they do.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP H&P
Procedure: total laparoscopic hysterectomy + BSO, planned 2/6 (gyn), for complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

Bleeding has tapered off since estradiol stopped 12/19. Hot flashes back, tolerable. Mood steady on escitalopram 10, still in counseling.
Functional capacity: climbs two flights and walks 30 min without symptoms (>4 METs). No chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, palpitations. No personal or family bleeding problems. No prior anesthesia trouble (several breast surgeries, lap chole). Never smoker. No OSA symptoms.

Meds: tamoxifen 20 (ask onc/gyn re peri-op hold given VTE risk), escitalopram 10, Ca/D, ibuprofen prn (stop 7 days before), MVI. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal. Airway unremarkable, full dentition. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Healed R mastectomy scar.

Labs today: CBC, BMP.

ASSESSMENT: Low-risk patient for a low-to-intermediate-risk procedure. No further cardiac testing needed; ECG not indicated. Medically optimized.
Tamoxifen peri-operative plan deferred to oncology and surgeon. Hold ibuprofen 1 week prior. Clearance faxed to gyn.

documents.title: Pre-op clearance faxed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pre-op note, CBC and BMP faxed to gynecology surgical scheduling. Confirmation received.

events.reason: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy

conditions.label: Complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia
conditions.note: Uterus removed; no carcinoma on final pathology.

conditions.label: Acquired absence of uterus and cervix

reports.text:
A. Uterus and cervix, total hysterectomy: uterus 112 g. Endometrium with complex atypical hyperplasia; no carcinoma identified after complete submission of the endometrium. Myometrium and serosa unremarkable. Cervix with no dysplasia.
B. Right ovary and fallopian tube: unremarkable ovary; unremarkable fallopian tube.
C. Left ovary and fallopian tube: unremarkable ovary; unremarkable fallopian tube.
reports.conclusion: Complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia without carcinoma. Benign cervix, both ovaries and both fallopian tubes.

documents.title: Operative summary
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Gynecologic Surgery - Operative and Discharge Summary
Date of surgery: 02/06/2024
Preoperative diagnosis: complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia; history of ER-positive breast cancer.
Procedure: total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.
Anesthesia: general. EBL 50 mL. No complications. Specimens to pathology.
Findings: uterus mildly enlarged, smooth. Normal-appearing tubes and ovaries. Pelvic and upper abdominal survey otherwise normal.
Course: voided, tolerated diet, ambulating; discharged home same evening.
Discharge medications: acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed; resume home medications.
Follow-up: gynecology post-op visit 2 weeks.
Final pathology (02/12): complex atypical hyperplasia, no carcinoma; tubes and ovaries benign. Discussed with patient by phone.

documents.title: Recovering
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Surgery went fine and the gynecologist says no cancer, which is a huge relief. The incisions look good. The hot flashes are back in full force though, I'm up two or three times a night changing my shirt. I know I can't go back on the estrogen. Anything else I can try?

documents.title: RE: Recovering
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wonderful news about the pathology. Hot flashes are expected now that your ovaries are out. The escitalopram you are already on helps some women with them. Layers, a fan by the bed and keeping the bedroom cool help too. Let's talk it through at your April visit, and keep a note of how many nights you're woken up.

10 wk out from TLH/BSO, healed, cleared by gyn. Hot flashes now 1-2 a night, she's sleeping better with the fan. Doesn't want another medication for them.
Mood: good. Counseling monthly now. PHQ-9 5. Escitalopram 10 - continue; psychiatry handed refills to us.
Weight back up to 69.5 kg.
Meds: tamoxifen, escitalopram, Ca/D, ibuprofen prn, MVI.
Exam: vitals fine. Abd: small laparoscopic incisions healed. Heart/lungs normal.
A/P
- S/p hysterectomy/BSO for atypical hyperplasia, benign path - done with gyn.
- Vasomotor sx after surgical menopause - nonpharmacologic, revisit prn.
- MDD recurrent - near remission, continue.
- Breast ca - tamoxifen per onc; mammogram due in June.
RTC October physical.

Left diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 06/20/2023.
Scattered fibroglandular density. Stable lumpectomy scar in the upper outer quadrant with expected architectural distortion. No mass, suspicious calcification or new asymmetry. Axillary tail unremarkable.

documents.body: This isn't my heart, it's on the right side where the mastectomy was. A dull ache that never quite goes away and sharp twinges when I move my arm. It has been going on for a few months. I've been taking ibuprofen 400 three times a day and it barely takes the edge off. I see oncology on September 9. Should I come in before?

documents.title: RE: Chest wall pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Janet, thanks for the detail. Please do raise this with oncology on the 9th - they will want to examine that area. Please don't go above the ibuprofen you're taking, and take it with food. If you'd like to be seen before then I have openings this week; just reply and the front desk will book you. If the pain changes, you get redness or swelling there, or you get short of breath, call us that day.

documents.title: RE: RE: Chest wall pain
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, I'll wait for the 9th.

documents.title: Medical oncology visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical Oncology - Clinic Note
Date of service: 09/09/2024
Patient: Janet Madden, 58F

Dx: R breast carcinoma stage IIA ER+ (2021) s/p lumpectomy/XRT, R MRM + ALND 02/2022, docetaxel/carboplatin 2022, adjuvant tamoxifen since 06/2022. Remote L breast IDC stage II (2018). S/p TLH/BSO 02/2024 for atypical hyperplasia (benign).

Interval: Seen today for right chest wall pain present for several months. She calls it a steady dull ache with occasional sharp jabs, worse with arm and trunk movement. Average 5/10, as high as 7/10 on bad days. Ibuprofen 400 mg TID gives her little relief. No fall, blow or other injury.

Meds: tamoxifen 20 mg daily, escitalopram 10 mg daily, calcium/vit D, ibuprofen, MVI. NKDA.

VS within normal limits.
Exam: R mastectomy site with mild tenderness to palpation along the lateral chest wall; no erythema, warmth or swelling. No palpable nodularity. L breast and both axillae without masses.

Labs today: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.8, plt 250, creatinine 0.9, LFTs normal.

A/P: Moderate cancer-related pain of the right chest wall, not controlled by NSAID alone.
- Add oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 mg, 1 tab q6h PRN; #40, no early refills. Continue ibuprofen with food. Bowel regimen with PEG 3350 daily PRN. Opioid agreement signed; PDMP reviewed.
- Continue tamoxifen.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Numbness. Had mild toe numbness since docetaxel/carboplatin in 2022, stable for years. Over the last ~6 wk it has spread: feet to above the ankles, and now both hands to the wrists. Describes it as gloves and socks. No pain, no burning, no weakness, no falls, no bladder/bowel change, no back pain. No new meds. Rare alcohol.
Meds: tamoxifen, escitalopram, oxycodone/APAP prn (~1/d), PEG, ibuprofen prn, Ca/D, MVI.

Exam: vitals ok. Strength 5/5 throughout incl. foot dorsiflexion. Vibration diminished at both great toes, present at the ankles. Ankle jerks absent bilaterally; knees 2+. Romberg negative. Gait normal, can heel and toe walk.

A/P: Worsening length-dependent sensory neuropathy, background of chemo neuropathy. B12, TSH, A1c today. Neurology referral. Foot checks daily, good footwear.

documents.title: Lab results to patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Janet, B12, thyroid and A1c are all normal, so none of the usual treatable causes showed up. The neurology referral is in; their office should call you within a week or two.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology Consultation
Date: 03/10/2025
Reason: numbness of the hands and feet

Thank you for referring Ms. Madden, a 59-year-old woman with ER-positive breast cancer on tamoxifen and a post-surgical right thoracic outlet syndrome. She says it feels as though she has gloves and socks on at all times, and this has steadily worsened over the last two months on a background of mild toe numbness since chemotherapy. She has no weakness and no pain. Her chemotherapy included docetaxel and carboplatin (2022).

Medications: tamoxifen, escitalopram, oxycodone/acetaminophen PRN, polyethylene glycol, ibuprofen PRN, calcium/vitamin D, multivitamin. Allergies: none.

Examination: Cranial nerves intact. Strength full. Vibration sense is reduced in both legs; joint position sense is preserved. Reflexes 1+ in the arms, 2+ at the knees, ankle jerks absent. Plantars flexor. Gait normal.

Recent B12, TSH and A1c from primary care are normal.

Impression: Length-dependent sensory polyneuropathy, attributable to her prior taxane/platinum chemotherapy, now worsening.

Recommendations: No medication needed while it remains painless. Daily foot inspection, protective footwear, fall precautions at night. Return if pain, weakness or gait change develops.

Neurology

events.reason: Right upper abdominal pain and weight loss

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: RUQ pain, weight loss.

HPI: Since mid-March a dull ache under the right ribs, slowly getting worse, now most of the day. Not related to meals. Weight 70.0 kg in Feb, 63.5 today without trying. No fever or chills. No jaundice, dark urine or pale stools noticed. Bowels unchanged on PEG. No nausea or vomiting. Chest wall pain is separate and stable. Gallbladder out years ago.

Meds: tamoxifen 20, escitalopram 10, oxycodone/APAP 5/325 prn, PEG, ibuprofen prn, Ca/D, MVI.

Exam: vitals normal, afebrile. Thinner. Sclerae anicteric. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness RUQ, no guarding, no palpable mass, liver edge not felt, no shifting dullness. No edema. No nodes.

A/P: RUQ pain + 6.5 kg weight loss in a woman with ER+ breast cancer - concerned. CMP, CBC today; abdominal ultrasound this week. Will call with results. Pain 4/10.

reports.text:
Complete abdominal ultrasound.
Indication: right upper quadrant pain, weight loss, history of breast cancer.
Liver: normal size. Multiple hypoechoic lesions are seen in both lobes, the largest in the right lobe measuring about 3 cm. Hepatic and portal veins patent with normal flow direction.
Gallbladder: surgically absent. Common bile duct 5 mm, not dilated for post-cholecystectomy status.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable. Spleen: normal size. Kidneys: normal size and echogenicity, no hydronephrosis. Aorta: normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Multiple hypoechoic liver lesions, concerning for metastatic disease given history. Cross-sectional imaging recommended.

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast

orders.reason: RUQ pain, weight loss, multiple liver lesions

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with US: several spots in the liver. Told her honestly that with her history the first concern is spread of the breast cancer, but we need a CT and likely a biopsy before anyone can say. ALP mildly up at 165, bilirubin normal, CBC normal. She took it calmly, asked good questions.
Plan: CT A/P with contrast (ordered, scheduling for next week). Urgent GI referral per our usual liver lesion workup. Messaged her oncologist with images/report so they are in the loop. Pt to call with fever, jaundice or worsening pain. Will call her after CT.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast, portal venous phase.
Comparison: ultrasound 04/30/2025.
Liver: multiple hypoattenuating masses in both lobes with irregular margins, the largest in segment 7 measuring 3.2 x 2.8 cm. Portal and hepatic veins patent.
Gallbladder: surgically absent. Biliary tree not dilated.
Pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands: normal. Kidneys enhance symmetrically; no hydronephrosis.
Bowel: no obstruction or wall thickening. No ascites. No enlarged lymph nodes.
Pelvis: post-hysterectomy; no adnexal mass. Bladder unremarkable.
Bones: no suspicious lesion.
Lung bases: clear.
reports.conclusion: Multiple irregular liver masses, most consistent with metastases in this patient with breast cancer. No other site of disease in the abdomen or pelvis.

documents.title: CT result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discussed CT with pt: multiple liver masses, nothing elsewhere in abdomen/pelvis. GI appt confirmed 5/13. Oncology aware and will see her after tissue diagnosis. She'd like to keep us updated by portal.

events.reason: Right upper quadrant pain, weight loss, liver masses

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology & Hepatology - New Consultation
Date of visit: 05/13/2025

Dear colleague,

Ms. Madden is a 59-year-old woman with breast cancer (left breast 2018, right ER-positive 2021, on tamoxifen) and a recent neurology evaluation for neuropathy, sent for right upper quadrant pain and liver masses. Over two months the RUQ pain has progressed and she has lost 10 kg without trying. She denies fevers, chills and any change in bowel habit. Remote cholecystectomy. NKDA.

Vital signs stable; weight 60.0 kg. Mild RUQ tenderness to palpation. No jaundice; no ascites. No stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Data: alkaline phosphatase mildly elevated, bilirubin normal. Ultrasound with multiple hypoechoic liver lesions; CT confirms multiple liver masses with irregular borders, no extrahepatic disease seen.

Impression: Multiple liver masses, almost certainly secondary malignancy, most likely metastatic breast carcinoma. No evidence of primary liver disease or biliary obstruction.

Plan: Ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a liver lesion arranged with interventional radiology for next week, with ER and HER2 testing requested. We will forward results to you and to her oncologist. No GI follow-up needed unless biopsy shows otherwise.

Gastroenterology

reports.text:
Specimen: liver, segment 7 lesion, ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (3 cores, 18-gauge).
Microscopic: cores of liver parenchyma infiltrated by nests and cords of malignant epithelial cells with moderate nuclear pleomorphism, in a desmoplastic stroma. Background liver unremarkable.
Immunohistochemistry: tumor cells positive for GATA3 and cytokeratin 7, negative for cytokeratin 20 and TTF-1. Estrogen receptor positive. HER2 negative (IHC 1+).
reports.conclusion: Liver, biopsy: metastatic carcinoma consistent with breast primary. ER positive, HER2 negative.

documents.title: Liver biopsy
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Interventional Radiology - Procedure Note (05/21/2025)
Procedure: ultrasound-guided percutaneous core biopsy, segment 7 liver lesion.
Consent obtained. Moderate sedation. INR and platelets acceptable. 18G coaxial, 3 cores, gelfoam tract embolization. No immediate complication. Observed 4 hours, discharged home.
Pathology (05/23): metastatic carcinoma consistent with breast primary, ER positive, HER2 negative. Results sent to ordering GI, oncology and PCP.

documents.title: Biopsy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Oncology called me Friday. It is the breast cancer in my liver. I see them next Tuesday to talk about treatment. I'm okay, mostly. I wanted you to hear it from me.

documents.body: Janet, thank you for telling me yourself. I'm so sorry. I've read the report. After you meet with oncology, let's sit down together - I'd like to hear how you're doing and make sure we have the rest of your care lined up around their plan. I'll have the front desk hold a slot for you in mid-June. Message me anytime before then.

Medical Oncology - Clinic Note
Date of service: 06/03/2025

Dx: Metastatic breast carcinoma to liver, ER+, HER2- (biopsy 05/21/2025), arising on adjuvant tamoxifen for R breast stage IIA ER+ cancer (2021). Remote L breast stage II IDC (2018). Surgically menopausal since BSO 02/2024.

We reviewed the biopsy and imaging; disease is limited to the liver. Goals of treatment discussed: not curable, treatable, aim is control and quality of life. She understands and wishes to proceed.

Plan:
- Stop tamoxifen.
- Start letrozole 2.5 mg daily and palbociclib 125 mg daily days 1-21 of 28.
- CBC on days 1 and 15 for the first two cycles, then monthly (neutropenia expected).
- Restaging CT in about 3 months.
- Baseline DXA (aromatase inhibitor) - requested from PCP.
- Continue oxycodone/APAP PRN, PEG.

Left diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 06/11/2024 and 06/20/2023.
Scattered fibroglandular density. Lumpectomy scar upper outer quadrant, unchanged. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion apart from the known scar.

Follow-up, liver mets.
Biopsy 5/21 metastatic breast ca, ER+/HER2-. Oncology stopped tamoxifen and started letrozole + palbociclib 6/3; cycle 1 going ok, a bit tired. RUQ ache 4/10, oxycodone/APAP 1-2/day. Weight 60.5 (60.0 at GI).
Mood: understandably shaken - crying more, sleep broken, still gardening some. PHQ-9 11, item 9 = 0. Declines a dose change for now; wants to restart counseling - gave her the oncology social work and therapist contacts.

A/P
1. Metastatic ER+ breast ca to liver - per onc.
2. MDD recurrent, worsened in context - counseling, continue escitalopram 10, recheck 2-3 mo.
3. Osteopenia + new AI - DXA ordered (onc request).
4. Pain - per onc, stable.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 02/27/2026, arrival 07:10 by ambulance
Patient: Janet Madden, 60F

CC: passed out at home this morning.

HPI: 60-year-old woman with metastatic ER+ breast cancer to the liver on letrozole and palbociclib. Weeks of worsening tiredness and lightheadedness on standing; this morning she stood up from the kitchen table, felt the room go gray and woke on the floor, no injury, no incontinence, no tongue biting, back to herself within a minute. She has been craving salt - salting everything, eating pickles from the jar. About 10 lb lost over the past two months. No chest pain, palpitations, fever, vomiting, diarrhea or bleeding.

Meds (per patient and pharmacy list): letrozole 2.5 mg daily, palbociclib 125 mg days 1-21, escitalopram 10 mg, oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 PRN, polyethylene glycol PRN, ibuprofen PRN, calcium/vitamin D, multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 90/60 supine, HR 102. Orthostatic: symptomatic with a fall in pressure on standing, test stopped. Thin, tired. Skin hyperpigmented, darkest in the palmar creases and the mastectomy and laparoscopic scars. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild RUQ tenderness. No focal neurologic deficit. No head injury.

Results: Na 128, K 5.5, Cl 95, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 65. 08:00 cortisol 3. Cosyntropin 250 mcg IV at 08:05; 60-minute cortisol 5. ACTH (drawn with the baseline cortisol) 486, resulted later in the day. ECG sinus tachycardia, no hyperkalemic changes. CT A/P: new bilateral adrenal masses (R 3.6 cm, L 4.1 cm) consistent with metastases; liver lesions smaller than in May.

ED course: D50 25 mL for glucose 65, then dextrose-containing saline. 2 L normal saline. Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV after the stimulation sample. BP 108/68, HR 84 by 12:30; dizziness improved.

Impression:
1. Adrenal insufficiency, primary, from bilateral adrenal metastases - adrenal crisis presentation.
2. Syncope due to #1.
3. Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia due to #1.
4. Metastatic breast cancer with new adrenal involvement.

Disposition: admitted to medicine.

Emergency Medicine

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (15 mg) on waking and 1 tablet (5 mg) at 2 PM. Double or triple doses on sick days as instructed.
Inject 100 mg into the thigh muscle once for vomiting, collapse or inability to take oral hydrocortisone, then call 911

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Discharge Summary - Hospital Medicine
Admitted 02/27/2026, discharged 03/02/2026

Principal diagnosis: adrenal crisis due to primary adrenal insufficiency from bilateral adrenal metastases.
Other: metastatic ER+/HER2- breast cancer (liver, now adrenals); depression; chemotherapy-induced neuropathy; osteopenia.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED after syncope with hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and hypoglycemia; 08:00 cortisol 3 with a 60-minute post-cosyntropin cortisol of 5 and ACTH 486, confirming primary adrenal insufficiency. CT showed new bilateral adrenal masses. Treated with hydrocortisone 50 mg IV every 6 hours and IV fluids, tapered to oral hydrocortisone on day 3, with fludrocortisone added for mineralocorticoid replacement. Orthostatic symptoms resolved and she walked the unit independently. Sodium 134 and potassium 4.6 on the day of discharge; glucose normal throughout after day 1. Endocrinology saw her in hospital and will follow as an outpatient. Oncology informed of new adrenal disease.

Discharge medications:
NEW hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg at 2 PM
NEW fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily
NEW hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg IM emergency kit (taught to self-inject)
CONTINUE letrozole 2.5 mg daily and palbociclib 125 mg days 1-21 pending oncology review; escitalopram 10 mg daily; oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 PRN; polyethylene glycol PRN; ibuprofen PRN; calcium/vitamin D; multivitamin.

Patient education: sick-day rules (double the hydrocortisone dose for fever or illness; triple for severe illness; injection and 911 if vomiting), medical alert ID, wallet steroid card provided.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; endocrinology 2 weeks; oncology 2-3 weeks. BMP at PCP visit.
Condition at discharge: good. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Transitional care outreach
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call (d/c 3/2, adrenal crisis). Pt home, says she feels 'like a person again'. No dizziness standing, eating and drinking well. Picked up hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone and the injection kit yesterday; reviewed timing 15 mg on waking / 5 mg at 2 pm. Reviewed sick-day doubling and when to use the shot. Has endo appt 3/12. TCM visit booked Thu 3/5 with PCP; BMP that day.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Admitted 2/27-3/2 after syncope at home: adrenal crisis from primary adrenal insufficiency, new bilateral adrenal mets on CT. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed in full.

Now: energy much better, no lightheadedness, salt craving gone, appetite good. Taking hydrocortisone 15 on waking / 5 at 2 pm and fludrocortisone 0.1 daily, alarms on her phone. Kit in her purse. Wearing a medical alert bracelet.
Meds reconciled: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, IM hydrocortisone kit, letrozole, palbociclib (onc to review), escitalopram 10, oxycodone/APAP prn, PEG prn, ibuprofen prn, Ca/D, MVI.

Exam: BP normal, no orthostatic drop sitting to standing. Wt 58.8. Skin still darker in creases and scars. Heart regular, lungs clear, mild RUQ tenderness, no edema.

BMP today: Na 137, K 4.3.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency (adrenal mets) - stable on replacement. Sick-day rules reviewed again with teach-back; she lives alone, so asked her to tell a neighbor where the kit is. Endo 3/12.
2. Metastatic breast ca, new adrenal progression - oncology appt pending.
3. Weight 58.8, recheck in 2 months.
4. Tdap due this year - at next visit.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology - Outpatient Consultation (03/12/2026)

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Madden after her admission for adrenal crisis. The biochemistry - low 08:00 cortisol of 3, flat response to cosyntropin (5 at 60 minutes), ACTH 486, potassium 5.5 with hyponatremia - together with the new bilateral adrenal metastases establishes primary adrenal insufficiency from metastatic replacement of both glands.

She is well on hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg at 2 pm with fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Seated blood pressure normal without postural drop. Sodium and potassium normal at her PCP visit.

Recommendations: continue current doses; adjust fludrocortisone by blood pressure, postural symptoms and potassium. Sick-day rules reinforced. Injection technique reviewed with a trainer device. Stress-dose coverage for procedures and any future surgery. Return in 3 months with BMP.

Endocrinology

medications.sig: 500 mg (two 250 mg injections) IM on days 1, 15 and 29, then every 28 days, given in oncology clinic

documents.title: Medical oncology visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical Oncology - Clinic Note
Date of service: 03/17/2026

Dx: Metastatic breast carcinoma, ER+/HER2-, liver (05/2025) and now bilateral adrenal glands (02/2026), with primary adrenal insufficiency.

Interval: hospitalized 02/27-03/02 with adrenal crisis; doing well on hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone. CT 02/27 shows new bilateral adrenal masses while the liver lesions continued to shrink - progression on letrozole/palbociclib after about 9 months.

Plan:
- Stop letrozole and palbociclib.
- Start fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1, 15, 29 then every 28 days; first dose given today. Stress dosing not required for injections.
- Restaging CT in 3 months.
- Continue pain regimen.

documents.title: Dentist and refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two things: I have a routine cleaning next week - do I need to take extra hydrocortisone for that? And I'm down to 10 days of the fludrocortisone, the hospital only gave me one month. Can you send it to my usual pharmacy?

documents.title: RE: Dentist and refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Janet - for a routine cleaning you don't need extra. If you ever need an extraction or anything under numbing that is more than a quick filling, check with endocrinology first; they may want a one-time extra dose. Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily, 90 days with refills, sent to your pharmacy. I sent the hydrocortisone too so they line up.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2-month f/u.
Adrenal insufficiency: hydrocortisone 15/5, fludro 0.1. No dizziness, no salt craving, no sick days so far. Endo happy.
Onc: fulvestrant since 3/17, injections monthly now; tolerating, mild soreness at injection sites. Restaging CT next month.
Pain 3/10, oxycodone/APAP a few times a week.
Mood: PHQ-9 6. Garden is going in. Continues escitalopram 10; counseling monthly.
Neuropathy unchanged.
Wt 60.5 (58.8 in March).

Exam: BP normal sitting and standing. Skin creases less dark. Heart/lungs normal. Abd soft, minimal RUQ tenderness. No edema.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency - stable. BMP today.
2. Metastatic ER+ breast ca on fulvestrant - per onc.
3. MDD recurrent - stable.
4. Tdap given today (last 2016).
RTC September, flu shot then.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. No reaction.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Endocrinology follow-up (06/11/2026): Doing well on hydrocortisone 15 mg/5 mg and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg. BP normal without postural drop; recent BMP normal. No change. Return in 6 months.
